project: Heritage Timber vs Timberthane: Which Beam Do You Need?

scenes.title: Hook
scenes.vo: Heritage Timber, or Timberthane? Two faux wood beam lines from Ekena Millwork. Here's how to choose.

scenes.title: What they share
scenes.vo: Both are lightweight, high-density polyurethane, with textures molded from real wood. Both are hollow, and both install the same way, over a wood block.

scenes.title: Lead time
scenes.vo: Need it fast? Heritage is Quick Ship. Stained beams usually ship in three to five business days. Timberthane is made to order, and usually ships in ten to twelve.

scenes.title: Sizes
scenes.vo: Heritage comes in eight set sizes, up to nine and a half by eleven and a half inches, and four to twenty-four feet long. Timberthane is built to your size: three to twenty-four inches, and up to thirty feet long.

scenes.title: Shapes
scenes.vo: Heritage is a three-sided U-beam. Timberthane also comes as a flat plank, an L-beam, or a four-sided box beam.

scenes.title: Textures and finishes
scenes.vo: Heritage has six textures and six hand-stained finishes, or primed to paint. Timberthane has eight textures and twenty-eight hand-finished colors.

scenes.title: Seams, endcaps, origin
scenes.vo: Heritage is molded in one piece, so its corners have no seams, and its endcaps ship separately, ready to stain. With Timberthane, you add endcaps when you order, and it's made in the U.S.A.

scenes.title: Which one
scenes.vo: A standard size, and need it soon? Go Heritage. It's the lower price, too. Need an exact size, another shape, or more colors? Go Timberthane.

scenes.title: End card
scenes.vo: Still deciding? Order a sample of each.
